Unique terminology vs other Nagara schools (Deul vs Shikhara)

Harihara deity (Shiva-Vishnu syncretism) - religious significance

UNESCO World Heritage Site - incomplete vimana, reasons for non-completion

Raha niche placement - central projections with deities
Parsvadevatas (subsidiary deities) - iconographic program
Alasa kanyas and salabhanjika figures - decorative elements

key_dimensions: Gujarat and Rajasthan distribution - regional extent

Rang Mandapa with elaborate ceiling - sculptural virtuosity
Jain Tirthankara iconography - religious specificity

concepts.name: Solanki School: Decorative and Sculptural Features
key_dimensions: Kirtimukha (face of glory) motifs - decorative elements
Toranas with intricate carvings - gateway ornamentation
Pillared halls with ornate brackets - structural decoration
Comparison with Odisha school - regional stylistic differences

concepts.name: Chandela School: Geographical and Historical Context
key_dimensions: Bundelkhand region (Madhya Pradesh) - geographical location

Khajuraho as primary center - concentration of monuments

concepts.name: Chandela School: Architectural Characteristics
key_dimensions: High platform (jagati) with subsidiary shrines - base structure
Sandhara type (circumambulatory path) - plan classification
Transept (mahamandapa) - cross-axial hall
Clustered shikharas with urushringa (subsidiary spires) - vertical composition

concepts.name: Khajuraho Temples: Typology and Classification
key_dimensions: Three groups: Western (Shaiva, Vaishnava), Eastern (Jain), Southern
Kandariya Mahadeva - largest and most ornate (Shaiva)
Lakshmana Temple - Vaishnava dedication, earliest Western group
Parsvanatha Temple - largest Jain temple in Eastern group

concepts.name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple: Architectural Pinnacle
key_dimensions: Mid-11th century construction - mature Chandela style
Panchayatana plan - main shrine with four subsidiary shrines
84 miniature spires on main shikhara - vertical multiplication
Three-part division: Ardhamandapa, Mahamandapa, Garbhagriha with Antarala

concepts.name: Khajuraho: Erotic Sculpture Interpretation
key_dimensions: Mithuna (amorous couples) placement - exterior walls only
Theories: Tantric influence, fertility symbolism, Kama as purushartha
Percentage of total sculpture - often exaggerated in popular perception
Comparison with Konark - stylistic and thematic differences

concepts.name: Chandela School: Sculptural Program and Iconography
key_dimensions: Three vertical bands: base moldings, wall sculptures, shikhara
Apsaras, surasundaris - celestial female figures
Vyala (mythical creatures) - decorative motifs
Narrative panels from epics and Puranas - religious storytelling

concepts.name: Comparative Analysis: Three Sub-schools
key_dimensions: Shikhara styles: Rekha Deul (Odisha) vs clustered (Solanki/Chandela)
Platform usage: absent in Odisha, prominent in Chandela
Material preferences: sandstone (Chandela), marble (Solanki), laterite/khondalite (Odisha)
Water architecture: Surya Kund (Solanki), absent in Chandela/Odisha temples

concepts.name: UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Nagara Sub-schools

concepts.name: Chronological Evolution and Decline
key_dimensions: Peak periods: Odisha (11th-13th century), Solanki (11th-12th century), Chandela (10th-11th century)

Transition to later styles - influence on subsequent architecture
